sentences.text: 3. As per the FIR for which the anticipatory bail is sought by the R/CR.A/1419/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 applicant, the applicant is shown as accused no. 3 Sureshbhai Patel.

As per the FIR, the first informant namely Raj Devendrabha Parmar has stated in the FIR that on 22.05.2023 he received a phone call from one of the friend of his father, that his father namely Sagarbhai @

sentences.text: Devendrabhai has consumed poison and therefore, at around 12:40 in the afternoon, he was taken to Civil Hospital, at Gandhinagar where he was admitted to ICU ward and he was unconscious.

During the treatment of his father, he found a chit while changing the clothes of his father wherein it was stated by father of the first informant that one Gurumaharaj Kiran Chauhan who has a temple in his residence had lended a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- to him and thereafter, despite repeated requests to repay the amount, he was not repaying the amount and followers of the aforesaid Gurumaharaj Chauhan including the present applicant have abused the deceased father of the complainant about his caste and threatened that if he seeks any recovery of the amount lended to the Gurumaharaj, the father of the complainant and his family would be killed.
Because of that, the deceased father of the complainant fell dejected and disreputed and therefore, he decided to end his life and ultimately committed suicide.
Though the poison was consumed on 22.05.2023, he died on 27.05.2023.

Therefore, son of the deceased Sagarbhai @ Devendrabhai - original complainant registered the FIR under R/CR.A/1419/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 sections 306, 406, 420, 506 (2) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code and under sections 3 (1) (R), 3 (2) (V) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Extent and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
4. Pursuant to the aforesaid FIR, as the present applicant is also arraigned as an accused no. 3, he has preferred this application for anticipatory bail.
5.

sentences.text: Learned advocate Mr. Patel submitted that it is true that the present applicant was follower of Gurumaharaj Chauhan but he was not knowing the deceased Sagarbhai @ Devendrabhai.

It was also submitted by learned advocate Mr. Patel that as the present applicant was not knowing the deceased Sagarbhai, there is no question of threatening him and at no point of time, he has threatened him or tried to stop him from recovering the amount which was allegedly lended by the deceased to the Gurumaharaj Kiran Chauhan.

In view of that, as the present applicant was a complete stranger to the transaction entered between the deceased person and Gurumaharaj Kiran Chauhan, the case against the present applicant was falsely registered and he is absolutely an innocent person.

It is also contended by learned advocate Mr. Patel that there are no past antecedents against the present applicant and he is a law abiding citizen and therefore, considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as considering the fact that R/CR.A/1419/2023 ORDER DATED:
21/06/2023 he was not the person who has received any amount from the deceased person nor he was recovering any amount on behalf of the Gurumaharaj Chauhan, he is not even remotely connected in the offence in question, therefore, he may be enlarged on bail.
6.

Learned APP Mr. Ronak Raval appearing for the respondent - State vehemently opposed the aforesaid application and submitted that the deceased consumed poison on 22.05.2023 and since then he was unconscious.
However, a suicide note was found from the complainant from the deceased father of the complainant while changing his clothes
wherein in the suicide note the incident about lending a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- to Gurumahrah Kiran Chauhan is narrated.

It is specifically stated by the deceased that whenever he tired to recover the aforesaid amount from the Gurumaharaj Kiran Chauhan, Gurumaharah Kiran Chauhan refused to pay back the aforesaid amount and the present applicant alongwith other followers of the Gurumaharaj threatened the present complainant - deceased father to kill himself and his family and also abused about his caste.
Feeling dejected, insulted and depressed about the aforesaid abused related to caste, the deceased Patel Sureshbhai Narsinhbhai vs State Of Gujarat on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2543305/
2 felt that there is no point in continuing leaving this life and therefore, he committed the suicide by consuming poison on 22.05.2023.

sentences.text:
Once he consumed the poison, he remained unconscious and ultimately died on 27.05.2023 in the morning at 06.50 and R/CR.A/1419/2023 ORDER DATED:
21/06/2023 thereafter, the FIR was registered at around 12:45 in the afternoon on the same day.
7.

Learned APP appearing for the respondent - State pointed out that the present applicant not only is named in the suicide note but also looking to the allegation against the present applicant, he was responsible for deceased in consuming poison as he used to threaten the deceased father of the complainant and was trying to stop the recovery of the amount from the deceased father of the complainant who was asking for paying back the amount he lended to Gurumaharaj Kiranbhai Chauhan.

8. Considering the prima facie evidence against the present applicant as he was named in the suicide note, this application being an application for anticipatory bail and as the investigation is going on,
leanred APP said that as the applicant is named in the suicide note, that is sufficient to reject the application for anticipatory bail as custodial interrogation of the present applicant would be required and by making the aforesaid submissions, he prayed for dismissal of this appeal.
9.
I have heard learned advocates for the parties and perused the record.

It is not in dispute that the applicant is named in the FIR on the basis of suicide note received from the clothes of R/CR.A/1419/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 the deceased person wherein specific allegations are levelled against the present applicant that he has not only abused the deceased father of the complainant but also threatened to kill him and his family and if he dares to ask for repayment of the amount which was lended by the deceased father of the complainant who lended a sum of Rs.
5,00,000/- to Gurumaharaj Chauhan.

10. Considering the fact that the present applicant is named in the FIR on the basis of suicide note received from clothes of the deceased father of the complainant, there is prima facie evidence against the present applicant whether the applicant was knowing the deceased father of the complainant or not and all other submissions made by learned advocate for the applicant are matter of evidence.

Today, when the investigation is going on, it would be too early to presume anything in favour of the present applicant but since, there is a suicide note wherein the the present applicant is specifically named and his role is also specifically stated at this juncture, I do not see any reason to entertain this appeal by granting anticipatory bail to the present applicant.
11. In view of above, the present appeal is required to be dismissed and the same is dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
